name: social-scheduler-mcp

tools.name: check_accounts
tools.description: Checks Chrome is reachable and lists the Facebook/Instagram and LinkedIn pages this user can post as, plus saved brand profiles. Read-only.

tools.name: read_recent_posts
tools.description: Reads the text of a page's most recent posts (used to learn a brand's voice). Read-only.

tools.name: get_brand_profile
tools.description: Returns the saved voice/style profile for a brand, if any, and the list of saved profiles.

tools.name: save_brand_profile
tools.description: Saves (overwrites) the markdown voice/style profile for a brand on this PC.

tools.name: prepare_post
tools.description: Fills in the post on each chosen platform and returns preview screenshots. DOES NOT publish or schedule. scheduleAt is local time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm (15 min to 28 days ahead); omit to publish immediately on confirm. Instagram requires at least one image. linkedinText optionally overrides text for LinkedIn.

tools.name: confirm_post
tools.description: Clicks the final Schedule/Publish button for a preview. ONLY call after the user has explicitly said "confirm" for this preview. Each preview can be confirmed once, within 30 minutes.

tools.name: cancel_post
tools.description: Discards a preview and closes its tabs without posting.

tools.name: list_scheduled
tools.description: Lists upcoming scheduled posts for a page. Read-only.

instructions:
Social Scheduler posts to Facebook Pages, Instagram and LinkedIn company pages through the user's own logged-in Chrome.

Always follow this routine:
1. If the page is unclear, call check_accounts and use the exact page name it returns.
2. Call get_brand_profile for the brand and write in that voice (offer to create one with read_recent_posts + save_brand_profile if none exists).
3. Show the draft text. Instagram needs an image (full file path); otherwise drop Instagram.
4. Convert times like "Friday 10am" to local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm. Omit scheduleAt only if the user wants it published now.
5. Call prepare_post and show every screenshot, the page, platforms and the "when" text. Check that each platform has its own correct date/time row.
6. Ask "Confirm?" and wait. Only call confirm_post after the user's explicit confirm for that exact preview. For changes, cancel_post and prepare again.
7. Report each platform's result. Never retry a failed post automatically; ask the user to check the platform first.

If a call seems to hang, Chrome is probably showing an "Allow" prompt for the debugging connection: ask the user to click Allow. Never type passwords; the user handles logins and security checks in Chrome. If a tool returns SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND, tell the user the site layout may have changed and that the plugin needs an update.
